prediction.likelyOutcome: Liability for the contact is effectively conceded, so this case is almost entirely a damages and causation trial. Plaintiff has credible treating-physician support (neurologist diagnosing post-concussion syndrome, radiologist finding TBI-consistent lesions) but faces a serious, well-supported defense built on malingering/effort testing and an extensive pre-existing comorbidity record, plus a nominal-damages jury instruction that meaningfully raises the chance of a modest compensatory verdict rather than the full $5.6 million requested. A mid-to-high six-figure to low seven-figure verdict is the most probable range, with real tail risk toward either the full life-care/pain-and-suffering ask or a sharply discounted/nominal award.

outcome.description: The jury, given a nominal-damages option at Walmart's request, awarded the claimant $1,000,000 in nominal damages and nothing for future medical expenses or pain and suffering; the claimant had asked for $5,596,168. The trial court entered judgment on the verdict and denied Walmart's motion for new trial arguing the nominal award was excessive as a matter of law. The Court of Appeals of Georgia affirmed on May 10, 2024. No attorney's fees.
